matched_title: GET /pulls/:id no longer triggers a GitHub refresh

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer triggers a GitHub refresh
findings.rationale: Previously, `GET /pulls/:id` attempted to fetch fresh data from GitHub and fell back to persisted data on failure. The new code removes the GitHub call entirely and always returns persisted data. While the response shape is identical, any caller that depended on the implicit refresh (e.g., expecting fresh data after a GitHub update) will now get stale data without any indication. The web client is updated to use the new `POST /pulls/:id/refresh` endpoint, but external callers are not.

matched_title: New field `reviewUrl` breaks the snake_case convention used by all other fields in `PrMeta`

findings.title: New field `reviewUrl` breaks the snake_case convention used by all other fields in `PrMeta`
findings.rationale: The stack context states that JSON fields are snake_case. Every other field in `PrMeta` (`cost_usd`, `latest_findings`, `score`, `updated_at`) follows that convention. Introducing a camelCase field (`reviewUrl`) is inconsistent and may confuse consumers that rely on a uniform naming pattern. Renaming to `review_url` would keep the contract predictable.

matched_title: GET /pulls/:id no longer fetches fresh data from GitHub, breaking callers that depend on implicit refresh

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer fetches fresh data from GitHub, breaking callers that depend on implicit refresh
findings.rationale: The old handler attempted a live GitHub fetch on every GET and fell back to persisted data only on failure. The new handler always returns persisted data without any GitHub call. Any caller that relied on the GET to return fresh data (e.g., e2e tests, CI runner, external consumers) will now get stale data until they explicitly call the new refresh endpoint. The PR only updates the web client; other callers are not updated. Furthermore, for PRs that have never been refreshed (e.g., old PRs, first-time views), the response will have empty `files` and `commits` arrays, which is a regression from the old behavior that would fetch the data on first view.
